[Theme 3 · Transdisciplinary research for management]{.theme-tag .tag-3}

At Oak Ridge National Laboratory, I developed geospatial frameworks to support planning for critical infrastructure and climate adaptation.
:::
:::

Projects included a multicriteria decision analysis for the strategic placement of reserve generators in Puerto Rico, planning green infrastructure placement using projected precipitation, estimating household electricity demand for urban infrastructure planning in select African countries, and exploring nighttime satellite imagery (VIIRS Day/Night Band) for monitoring power recovery.

## Key insights

- Physical landscape attributes, socioeconomic conditions, and environmental factors jointly shape vulnerability, so siting decisions benefit from integrating all three.
- Incorporating climate projections helps target infrastructure where future needs will be greatest.

## Methods & tools

GIS-based multicriteria decision analysis · climate projections · VIIRS nighttime lights · R · Python · ArcGIS
